topic: Unknown coefficient from a system's intersection point
problem: -x - wy = -337 and 2x - wy = 47. The graphs of these two equations intersect at the point (q, 19). What is the value of w?

bad.why: Substituting y=19, subtracting to get q, and back-solving for w is several hand steps that one bracket regression replaces.
Graphing -q-19w=-337 and 2q-19w=47 treats q and w as plot axes; Desmos only graphs x and y, so those rows error.

algebraFirst.description: Substitute y=19 into both equations, subtract them to get 3q=384, solve q=128, then back-substitute to get w=11.

explanationNotes: Explain that the meeting point (q, 19) means both equations are true when x=q and y=19, so putting 19 in for y gives two conditions on q and w. Desmos solves them together with ~ (both brackets fitted at once); q is just the unknown x-coordinate, not something to graph as an axis.
notes: Substitute y=19 and fit q,w via [-q-19w,2q-19w]~[-337,47]; never graph q or w as if they were plotting axes (Desmos only has x,y coordinates).
